Pins the residual-only cooperative epilogue on the subgroup-matrix 1x1 route. The residual is present while the activation attribute is omitted.

Zero-length batch axis N of X (empty NCHW input). ONNX treats empty tensors as first-class; W/bias-driven channel dims stay normal and Y=[0,outC,Hout,Wout] => EMPTY output. 2x2 conv, no bias, with the optional activation omitted.
A non-empty float16 witness for both optional tensor inputs. Exact binary-fraction values make the bias and residual additions independently visible without activation rounding noise.
The 3x3 biased convolution produces 64 register tiles, exercising the register-tiled im2col GEMM specialization at its shared workgroup floor.
The biased 1x1 convolution produces 64 register tiles, exercising the register-tiled direct GEMM specialization at its shared workgroup floor.
A negative-infinity residual drives every clipped position to the activation minimum whatever the convolution produced, so the activation and weight fills are uniform.

A compact 3x3 convolution with 64 input and output channels exercises an aligned im2col reduction and its no-subgroups fallback.

A 3x3 Relu convolution from 32 input channels to 256 output channels over a 32x32 image exercises the 128-lane register-blocked im2col multiplication.
FusedConv inherits Conv auto_pad semantics. SAME_UPPER with stride 2 requires trailing padding and a 2x2 output here, exercising padding derived from the official auto_pad and strides attributes.

provenance.notes: A volumetric case evaluates `Relu(Conv3D(X, W))` through the generic three-dimensional convolution loop and fused activation epilogue.

Volumetric bias + LeakyRelu with an asymmetric depth pad, so the fused epilogue and the front-pad guard of the 3D loop nest run together. The weights and bias are chosen so the pre-activation output straddles zero: with an all-positive output LeakyRelu is the identity and the fixture would not see the activation at all.
A volumetric residual computes `Y = Relu(Conv3D(X, W) + Z)` with `Z` exactly matching the output shape.
A grouped rank-5 volumetric convolution exercises per-group channel indexing and the plain no-activation output store.

The fourth corner of the volumetric family: bias and residual together, under a Sigmoid whose output is bounded away from the linear region so the epilogue order (conv + B + Z, then activate) is visible.
A large NCW convolution with bias and HardSwish exercises register-tiled implicit multiplication.
A strided NCW convolution over an odd input width exercises unbiased register-tiled multiplication with HardSwish.

Non-1x1 kernel keeps the 1x1 subgroup-matrix shortcut out, so the exact (unpadded) im2col subgroup-matrix GEMM owns the z-residual epilogue. 2x2 over 8 channels lands kernelRows=32 and outputPixels=64, both on the alignment the exact path requires.
A biased 2x2 convolution with `kernelRows = 32` and 64 output pixels exercises the exact im2col subgroup-matrix GEMM without a residual input.
A 2x2 convolution with 49 output positions, residual input, and fused Relu checks the final partial output tile.
group != 1 fails the dense-group contract every im2col/1x1 GEMM route requires, leaving the direct unrolled kernel to carry the z-residual epilogue.

Grouped 3x3 convolution with bias and z-residual checks the complete epilogue order: bias, residual, then activation.

ORT builds x*sigmoid(alpha*x) after a Conv and checks the fused result against the unfused graph on random data in [-3,3]; transcribed here with the same shapes and a deterministic fill. alpha 1.4 as in the upstream test.
With alpha 1, QuickGelu computes x*sigmoid(x); the expected values distinguish it from other activation settings.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: value * sigmoid(alpha*value), alpha default 1.702; alpha==1 is SiLU/Swish. alpha == 1 is a distinct case because the multiply drops out. Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: select(alpha*(exp(v)-1), v, v >= 0). Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: 0.5*v*(1+erf(v/sqrt2)); ORT encodes the approximation mode as activation_params[0] = 0 (erf) or 1 (tanh) and emits an Abramowitz-Stegun 7.1.26 erf helper as a module-scope declaration. Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: v*(0.5 + 0.5*tanh_safe(v*(0.035677408136300125*v*v + 0.79788456080286535))); ORT reaches it as Gelu with activation_params[0] == 1 or as FastGelu, and uses an overflow-safe tanh because WGSL tanh returns NaN for large inputs. Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: max(v,0) + log(1 + exp(-abs(v))) -- the overflow-safe form. Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.

Transcribed from ORT's fused activation set. Formula: select(0, v, v > alpha), alpha default 1.0. Shapes follow RunWebGpuConvActivationParity (x [1,4,14,14], w [8,4,3,3], bias [8], input spanning [-3,3] so asymmetric activations see both signs); the upstream test uses random data, replaced here with a deterministic fill.
